Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're preparing our internal runbook for the PrivCP cutover and need specific answers on a couple of items before we sign off on the network cutover window:

1) SCIM mapping: ACME requires group-to-role mappings that preserve our least-privilege model. Can you confirm whether the PrivCP SCIM adapter supports
   - dynamic group sync (delta only)
   - nested groups mapping (we have nested groups in Azure AD)

2) Operator role lifecycle: we want short-lived operator elevation (time-boxed) with automatic revocation. Is there a recommended TTL pattern (e.g., 8h, 24h) and does Redwood expose a token TTL that integrates with our ticketing system for approvals?

3) Audit & retention: For compliance we need per-operation audit identity (who elevated, which instance, which model) retained for 365 days. Does the private control plane ship these logs to our SIEM or do we need to configure a forwarder?

I've attached a brief spreadsheet with our proposed mappings and a sample SAML metadata stub. Please review and call out any blockers. We aim to lock the operator provisioning approach by 2026-12-10.

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. I reviewed the spreadsheet and sketched an initial operational pattern. Attached is an updated mapping (privcp-access-mapping.xlsx) and a short diff of our SCIM schema expectations (scim-schema-diff.txt). Highlights below: 

- SCIM sync mode: Redwood's private SCIM connector supports incremental delta syncs and full resyncs. Delta sync is the default and has been tested against Azure AD and Okta for customers with ~50k identities. We include an attribute 'redwood_role' that maps to PrivCP operator roles.

- Nested groups: We do support nested group flattening during sync. The connector exposes a mapping rule that you can toggle: flatten (default) or preserve hierarchy. For ACME I'd recommend flatten + attribute tag to reduce role explosion.

- Operator TTL: We recommend a ticket-driven ephemeral role model. Implementation options:
  * Short-lived membership via SCIM (preferred): Provision SCIM membership that expires after X hours (supports 8h and 24h patterns).
  * Token-based elevation: Use the PrivCP elevation API to mint a short-lived operator token (default 8h). Token TTL is configurable per-tenant up to 30 days.

- Approval flow: We can webhook into your ticketing system (Jira/ServiceNow) for approvals; once ticket is approved the provisioning flow will add the SCIM membership and set TTL.

- Audit logs: PrivCP emits per-action audit events (actor, subject, resource, action, model_id, request_id). For Private deployments we install a forwarder that ships logs to customer SIEM (syslog / JSON over TLS). Retention is configurable; we can set the default retention to 365 days in your account config.

Open questions for you:
- Which approval system should we target for the webhook (ticket queue name / project)?
- Are you comfortable with flattening nested groups? If not, we can prepare an example mapping to preserve the hierarchy.

Next steps: I attached the mapping and schema diff. Ben will propose role binding templates and policy snippets. After your confirmation we'll produce a cutover runbook and a pre-cutover acceptance checklist.

Thanks,

Aisha/Mina — couple of practical notes and a recommended role-binding template. I'm pasting the important bits here to make the plan concrete.

1) SCIM performance: For delta sync we recommend a polling cadence of 60s for AD/Okta connectors for large orgs. That gives near-real-time behavior without overwhelming the connector. We'll provide metrics in the console so you can tune it.

2) Role-binding template (example YAML):
   - role: privcp.operator
     scopes: [instances:write, models:list, audits:read]
     conditional: { network: ["vpc-12345"], mfa: true }
     ttl_hours: 8

   We'll include a higher-privilege break-glass role with an audit trigger and manual approval.

3) Token model pros/cons:
   - SCIM membership TTL: better for compliance because membership changes are recorded in directory history.
   - Token elevation: faster, better UX for short spikes, but requires strict handling of token storage on the client-side.

4) SAML metadata: Alice from CloudVendor, can you confirm that we can consume ACME's metadata with the following assertion mapping? (email -> userPrincipalName, groups -> groups claim)

5) Audit forwarding: We'll deploy a lightweight forwarder in your VPC that talks to your SIEM over TLS. It buffers locally and ships with guaranteed delivery semantics (retry + backpressure). We recommend configuring a dedicated intake endpoint and account for separation of logs.

Action items I propose now:
- ACME: confirm ticket queue for webhook (Aisha)
- ACME: confirm group flattening preference
- Redwood: provide role-binding YAML and cutover checklist (we'll have a PR by 2026-12-06)

I'll attach the role-binding template and an internal runbook draft to the shared Drive link.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
